    A mutation probe that makes the target module fail to COMPILE or the test file fail COLLECTION must be classified NOT-A-KILL, never KILLED: pytest exits nonzero for a collection error exactly as it does for assertion failures, so exit code alone cannot distinguish them. Observed on hyperv-mcp issue #23: a mutation harness applied a replacement that produced a SyntaxError, the check 'failed' on collection, and the trace's evidence table recorded KILLED - but an independent reviewer re-ran a well-formed version of the same mutant and it SURVIVED, so the shipped evidence contained a false row contradicting the run's own prose. Protocol for any mutation harness: (1) after applying the mutant, import the mutated module (or run pytest and grep stdout for 'error during collection'/'SyntaxError') BEFORE recording a verdict; (2) a KILLED verdict requires the named check to fail ON ITS ASSERTIONS with mutated-but-compiling code; (3) include a positive control - demonstrate the harness reports SURVIVED when the mutation is semantically inert; (4) when a review's evidence table and its own prose disagree, treat the table as suspect until re-executed.
    tags: mutation-testing,malformed-mutant,collection-error,not-a-kill,positive-control,issue-tracer,evidence-integrity
